targetAudience.primary: Engineering leads building long-horizon agent software workflows
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands code revisions, testing, role separation, and agent context windows.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Project continuity is being represented by model context or prose summaries, so acceptance evidence can lose its exact candidate identity after later changes.

whyNow: A primary Harness-of-Harness study separates planning, development, and QA across repeated role invocations while carrying artifact state and evidence state independently across loops; its multi-day case also records defects reopening after later regressions.

externalHook.description: A defect can be legitimately closed against one candidate revision and legitimately reopen after later changes, showing that acceptance belongs to a candidate, not to a conversation or issue label forever.

coreProposition: Context is disposable but project truth is not: long-horizon agent engineering needs stable candidate identity, separate durable artifact and evidence state, independent acceptance, and explicit freshness invalidation after change.

originalValue.description: Turns the study's role and state separation into four inspectable identities—candidate, artifact state, evidence state, and role authority—so recovery and acceptance do not depend on conversational memory.

readerTakeaway: Bind every test and acceptance claim to an exact candidate revision, persist unresolved obligations and evidence outside model context, separate implementation from acceptance, and invalidate affected evidence after later changes.

supported: The study separates planning, development, and QA role invocations and carries artifact state and evidence state independently across loops.
The study reports benchmark improvements in the examined harness-model configurations.
The multi-day case preserves versioned project and evidence history and records issues reopening after later regressions.
unsupported: That role separation alone provides full statistical independence
That the reported benchmark gains generalize to all software engineering
That the architecture by itself guarantees crash consistency, exactly-once effects, security, or production correctness
uncertain: How to automatically invalidate only evidence affected by a later change
When different models, deterministic tests, human review, or external evaluation are required for stronger independence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The engineering argument is derived from external primary research and remains independently useful without first-party projects.

decisionReason: The evidence supports a bounded, practical state-and-acceptance model for long-horizon agent engineering without turning benchmark outcomes into universal claims.
